contradictions.what: Rep says nothing got silence and it was a good cycle, yet a value analysis went undone and the champion's business-case request went unmet.
Rep says Lucy was sold and no value figure was needed, but the CFO decided and rejected on 'same thing'.
Rep says the rate killed it and more rate room wins, but admits Martin might still see 'same rate' and IT was nervous about timing.
Rep says it isn't 'the same thing' but nothing from us showed Martin the difference; uplift was generic.
Lucy called it a formality before the meeting, then Martin rejected it; the champion misjudged the decider.
Bank offered 'no new product, just a better rate', yet rate is framed as our loss on price; 'same rate' point at T34 implies parity was possible.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Said 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed' and moved to 'we lost on price' instead of naming a silent part.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get?
dodges.what: Answered with the generic uplift slide; admitted only when pressed that no Fernbrook figure existed.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Paused, said 'Nothing from us', then assumed Lucy told him.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Gave the business-case request but framed it as sending the deck and pricing, not acknowledging the gap.
